authors: Eitan Altman
venue: Routledge (Stochastic Modeling; 2021 digital edition - original 1999 printing not verified via API)
problem: Formal theory of Markov decision processes with additional expected (discounted/average) cost constraints (CMDPs).
method: Monograph; chapter titles in the Crossref record include 'Markov decision processes', 'Convergence of discounted constrained MDPs' and 'Sensitivity analysis'.
environment_or_data: n/a (theory)
key_results: Standard reference that defines the CMDP setting used by CPO/Lagrangian safe RL.
limitations: Only bibliographic metadata and chapter list were accessible (no abstract/full text); cite only as the canonical CMDP definition.

authors: Joshua Achiam; David Held; Aviv Tamar; Pieter Abbeel
problem: Policy search for RL with safety constraints expressed as expected cumulative costs.
method: Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO): trust-region policy update with a constraint on the expected cost; relies on a new bound relating the returns of two policies to their average divergence.
environment_or_data: Simulated robot locomotion tasks with safety-motivated constraints
key_results: Qualitative: near-constraint satisfaction at each policy iteration, guarantees on policy behaviour throughout training (per abstract).
limitations: Guarantee concerns expected cost and is approximate ('near-constraint satisfaction'); no per-step/per-state feasibility.

authors: Chen Tessler; Daniel J. Mankowitz; Shie Mannor
problem: Constrained RL where reward misspecification is avoided by explicit constraints.
method: Reward Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO): multi-timescale Lagrangian approach in which a learned penalty signal (multiplier) steers the policy toward constraint satisfaction.
environment_or_data: not read (abstract only)
key_results: Qualitative: convergence of the multi-timescale scheme is proved; empirical evidence of constraint-satisfying policies.
limitations: Convergence is asymptotic and the constraint is on (discounted/average) cost; violations can occur during training.

authors: Gal Dalal; Krishnamurthy Dvijotham; Matej Vecerik; Todd Hester; Cosmin Paduraru; Yuval Tassa
problem: Never violating hard state constraints while an RL agent learns on a physical system (e.g., data-centre cooling, robots).
method: Safety layer added to the policy that analytically solves a per-state action-correction problem; closed form obtained via a linearised constraint model learned from logged data.
environment_or_data: New physics-based environments
key_results: Zero constraint violations reported where reward shaping fails (abstract).
limitations: Safety relies on an approximate learned linear model; the closed form is commonly noted to assume a single active constraint at a time (as summarised by su2025review).

authors: Mohammed Alshiekh; Roderick Bloem; Ruediger Ehlers; Bettina Koenighofer; S. Niekum; U. Topcu
problem: Learning optimal policies while enforcing safety properties written in temporal logic during learning and execution.
method: Shield: a reactive system synthesised from the temporal-logic specification that monitors the learner's actions and corrects them only when they would violate the specification; conditions under which convergence guarantees are preserved are discussed.
architecture: Shield in the loop of a generic RL learner
environment_or_data: Several RL scenarios (not detailed in abstract)
key_results: Qualitative: specification enforced during learning and execution by construction of the shield.
limitations: Requires a (typically discrete/abstracted) model of safety-relevant dynamics; guarantee holds w.r.t. that abstraction.

authors: Yujia Wang; Zhe Wu
problem: Safe RL for optimal control of nonlinear systems with input constraints.
method: Control Lyapunov-barrier function (CLBF) embedded in the performance index; NN approximates the CLBF-based value function from data on safe/unsafe operation.
environment_or_data: Chemical process example
key_results: Theoretical results on stability, safety and optimality that account for NN approximation error (abstract).
limitations: Barrier-based method shapes the value/cost rather than projecting actions; process-control case only.

authors: Shangding Gu; Long Yang; Yali Du; Guang Chen; Florian Walter; Jun Wang; Alois Knoll
venue: IEEE Trans. Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
problem: Survey of safe RL methods, theory and applications.
method: Review organised around five questions ('2H3W'); classifies methods (primal-dual/Lagrangian, trust-region CPO family, formal methods/shielding, Lyapunov, Gaussian-process) and constraint types (cumulative, instantaneous, state-based).
environment_or_data: Benchmarks: AI Safety Gridworlds, Safety Gym, Safe Control Gym, multi-agent safe benchmarks
key_results: Distinguishes cumulative (discounted, mean, probabilistic) from instantaneous constraints (Sec. 2.2); notes that few safety-layer methods offer rigorous guarantees during training.
limitations: Power/energy applications only lightly covered; action-projection layers treated briefly.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.10330 (arXiv version of the TPAMI article) ; https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/batch (abstract field)

authors: John Schulman; Filip Wolski; Prafulla Dhariwal; Alec Radford; Oleg Klimov
problem: Simple, sample-efficient on-policy policy-gradient optimisation.
method: Proximal Policy Optimization: clipped surrogate objective allowing multiple epochs of minibatch updates per batch.
environment_or_data: Simulated robotic locomotion, Atari
baselines: Other online policy-gradient methods incl. TRPO (abstract)
key_results: Outperforms other online policy-gradient methods with favourable sample complexity/simplicity trade-off (abstract).
limitations: No constraint handling; constraints must be added (penalty, Lagrangian, or action layer).

authors: Tuomas Haarnoja; Aurick Zhou; Pieter Abbeel; Sergey Levine
problem: Sample-efficient, stable off-policy deep RL for continuous control.
method: Soft Actor-Critic: maximum-entropy off-policy actor-critic with a stochastic actor.
architecture: Actor-critic (stochastic policy, twin Q not in abstract)
environment_or_data: Continuous-control benchmarks
key_results: State-of-the-art results and stability across seeds (abstract).
limitations: No constraint handling.

authors: Scott Fujimoto; Herke van Hoof; David Meger
problem: Overestimation bias from function approximation in actor-critic methods.
method: TD3: clipped double-Q (minimum of two critics), delayed policy updates, link between target networks and overestimation.
environment_or_data: OpenAI Gym continuous-control tasks
baselines: State of the art at the time
key_results: Outperforms the state of the art on every tested environment (abstract).
limitations: No constraint handling; base learner used by several safety-layer papers (ceusters2023adaptive, markgraf2025safe, kasaura2023benchmarking).

authors: Brandon Amos; J. Zico Kolter
problem: Embedding constrained optimisation as a layer of a deep network.
method: OptNet: quadratic programs as layers; exact gradients via sensitivity analysis/implicit differentiation of the KKT conditions; batched GPU primal-dual interior-point solver.
environment_or_data: Synthetic tasks; mini-Sudoku
key_results: Backprop gradients at almost no extra cost on top of the solve; learns hard constraints (mini-Sudoku) (abstract).
limitations: Not an RL paper; layer output is feasible because it is an exact QP solution (up to solver tolerance); per-step cost of an iterative solve.

authors: Akshay Agrawal; Brandon Amos; Shane Barratt; Stephen Boyd; Steven Diamond; J. Zico Kolter
problem: General-purpose differentiation through disciplined convex programs.
method: Disciplined parametrized programming and affine-solver-affine form; analytical differentiation implemented in CVXPY 1.1 with PyTorch/TensorFlow layers (cvxpylayers).
environment_or_data: Applications incl. linear machine learning models (abstract truncated)
key_results: Lowers the barrier to using convex programs in differentiable pipelines (abstract).
limitations: Generic solver-based layer; per-call solve cost (cf. 8.6 ms projection vs 4.5 ms network reported by chen2021enforcing; large overhead in kasaura2023benchmarking).

authors: Priya L. Donti; David Rolnick; J. Zico Kolter
problem: Fast approximate solution of optimisation problems with hard constraints by neural networks.
method: DC3: completion of partial solutions to satisfy equality constraints and unrolled gradient-based correction for inequality constraints, both differentiable.
environment_or_data: Synthetic optimisation tasks; AC optimal power flow
key_results: Near-optimal objective values while preserving feasibility (abstract).
limitations: Inequality feasibility relies on a finite number of correction steps (not a closed-form projection); not RL.

authors: Meiyi Li; Soheil Kolouri; Javad Mohammadi
problem: Neural approximators for optimisation problems with hard linear constraints.
method: Reduce to independent variables, construct a gauge function mapping the l-infinity unit ball onto the reduced feasible polytope, learn a 'virtual' point in the ball, gauge-map it to a feasible point, recover dependent variables.
environment_or_data: not read (abstract only)
key_results: Feasible, nearly optimal solutions in a single forward pass (abstract).
limitations: Abstract-level reading only; linear constraints; not an RL paper; proof details not checked.

authors: Bingqing Chen; Priya L. Donti; Kyri Baker; J. Zico Kolter; M. Berges
venue: Proc. 12th ACM Int. Conf. Future Energy Systems (e-Energy '21)
problem: RL policies for energy systems whose actions must satisfy convex operational constraints (building HVAC, inverter voltage control).
method: PROF: differentiable projection layer onto an approximate convex constraint set (Euclidean projection, Eq. 7) inside the policy; gradients via implicit differentiation of KKT conditions (Sec. 3.2, Eqs. 8-9); auxiliary loss lambda*||pi - pi_hat||^2 between pre- and post-projection actions (Eq. 16).
architecture: Building: LSTM Gaussian policy trained with PPO; inverters: utility-level + per-inverter networks trained by differentiating through a linearised grid model
environment_or_data: EnergyPlus 600 m2 building (Pittsburgh weather); IEEE 37-bus feeder with 21 PV inverters, 1-s steps over a week
baselines: Building: P-controller, Gnu-RL, Agent #6, 'LSTM & Clip' ablations; inverters: IEEE 1547.8 Volt/Var, optimum of linearised model, AC-OPF optimum
key_results: Heating demand 33,271 vs 34,687 kW (about 4% saving vs Gnu-RL); Volt/Var violates voltage limits 22.3% of the time vs 0% for PROF; projection 8.6 ms vs network 4.5 ms (Sec. 5.3, 6.3, 7).
limitations: Feasibility only w.r.t. an approximate (linearised) constraint set; building comfort violated when control saturates; per-step solver cost; no scaling study in number of devices.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.08881 (arXiv version of the e-Energy paper)

authors: Sebastien Gros; Mario Zanon; Alberto Bemporad
problem: Whether projecting RL actions onto a safe set disrupts learning and optimality.
method: Analysis for Q-learning (projection of greedy policy is generally suboptimal; fix: constrained minimisation of Q with restricted TD targets, Lemma 1) and for policy gradients: deterministic case uses the projected-policy Jacobian M(x) (null-space projector of active constraints, Prop. 1/Cor. 1); stochastic case uses the score of the unprojected sample with the advantage of the projected action (Prop. 2); extension to robust-MPC projections (Cor. 2-3).
environment_or_data: Linear system with circular state constraint; robust linear MPC as projection (Sec. 6)
key_results: Unbiased policy-gradient corrections under LICQ/SOSC; qualitative convergence plots only.
limitations: Assumes LICQ and strict SOSC; stochastic result is asymptotic (barrier parameter -> 0); single small example.

authors: Kazumi Kasaura; Shuwa Miura; Tadashi Kozuno; Ryo Yonetani; Kenta Hoshino; Y. Hosoe
problem: Benchmarking action-constrained RL (each action must satisfy constraints) in robotics control.
method: Compares closest-point projection with critic on projected (DPro) or pre-projected actions (DPre), differentiable optimisation layer (DOpt via cvxpylayers), Frank-Wolfe (NFWPO), alpha-projection, radial squashing, and penalty variants (Sec. III-IV).
environment_or_data: MuJoCo-type robotics tasks (Reacher, HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker) with box, L2-ball, weighted linear-sum upper bounds, sums of positive parts, quadratic and state-dependent constraints
key_results: Training the critic on pre-projected actions (DPre/SPre, + penalty) is a strong simple baseline; DOpt has large runtime overhead without clear gains; zero-gradient problem of projection explicitly discussed (Sec. III-A, IV-E).
limitations: Robotics only; DOpt limited by cvxpylayers support and run at reduced batch size; four environments.

authors: Hannah Markgraf; Shambhuraj Sawant; Hanna Krasowski; Lukas Schaefer; Sebastien Gros; Matthias Althoff
problem: Whether a projection safeguard should be part of the environment (SE-RL) or of the policy as a differentiable layer (SP-RL).
method: Unified actor-critic formalisation of SE-RL and SP-RL; Theorem 1 (optimal value functions coincide), Lemma 1 (equivalence for stochastic policies with GAE), Lemma 2 (action aliasing: actions in the normal cone map to the same safe action -> rank-deficient Jacobian), Lemma 3 (flat-lining critic in SE-RL); mitigation via reward penalty (SE-RL), per-sample loss and a new penalty critic (PenC) for SP-RL (Sec. 5-7).
environment_or_data: Pendulum and quadrotor stabilisation (RCI sets), seeker navigation (state-dependent safe set), building energy-management task
baselines: Vanilla vs improved SE-RL and SP-RL variants
key_results: A2C: SE-RL = SP-RL; TD3: vanilla SE-RL often beats vanilla SP-RL, improved SP-RL matches or beats penalised SE-RL; improved SP-RL costs about 3-12x SE-RL compute (Sec. 8-9).
limitations: Preprint; PPO/SAC not analysed; safety by construction of the projection onto given safe sets (theorems concern learning, not safety).

authors: Tong Su; Tong Wu; Junbo Zhao; Anna Scaglione; Le Xie
problem: Review of safe RL methods for power-system operation and control.
method: Taxonomy (Sec. III, Fig. 4): penalised reward; learning-process modification (Lagrangian/primal-dual, Lyapunov, Gaussian process, barrier function, robust RL); RL-structure adjustment (projection/trust region, shielding, safety layer); Table II compares pros/cons.
environment_or_data: Power-system applications: security control, real-time operation, planning, emerging areas
key_results: Classifies projection, Lyapunov, shielding and (strictly applied) safety layers as hard-constraint methods and Lagrangian, barrier, GP as soft/probabilistic (Sec. III-I); scalability of projection/safety layers flagged as a barrier.
limitations: Visible text did not discuss gradients through projection or differentiable optimisation layers; EV subsection truncated in our reading.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.00304 (arXiv version; read up to Sec. IV)

authors: Daniel Tabas; Baosen Zhang
problem: Safe RL for frequency regulation with guaranteed state constraints and no online projection/MPC.
method: Closed-form, differentiable safety filter: gauge map from the l-infinity unit ball onto the state-dependent safe action polytope derived from a robust controlled-invariant (RCI) polytope plus linear backup K x (Sec. III, Eq. 12-13, Thm. 1); trained end-to-end with DDPG.
architecture: DDPG actor (2x256 ReLU, sigmoid output) + gauge-map layer
environment_or_data: Modified 9-bus system with 3 synchronous generators, 3 IBRs, 3 loads (0.05 s steps)
baselines: Robust linear feedback; DDPG with constraint-violation penalties
key_results: Learned policy has lower cost than robust linear feedback with the same safe set; penalty-DDPG leaves the safe set in training and violates constraints at test (Figs. 5-7, no numeric counts).
limitations: Linear dynamics with bounded disturbances; RCI set computed offline by SDP; single small test system; no timing comparison.

authors: Glenn Ceusters; Muhammad Andy Putratama; Ruediger Franke; Ann Nowe; M. Messagie
problem: Safe RL with hard constraints for multi-energy management systems where constraint functions are imperfectly known.
method: OptLayerPolicy: QP projection (OptLayer) of the proposed action onto the constraint set, switching to a hand-designed SafeFallback policy if the projection distance exceeds a threshold; self-improving constraints via learned MLP residuals (Sec. 3, Alg. 1-2).
architecture: TD3 (Stable-Baselines) + external QP safety layer (projected action sent to environment, no gradient through the QP)
environment_or_data: Simulated multi-energy system: grid, 0.8 MWe wind, 1.0 MWe PV, gas boiler, heat pump, CHP, 3.5 MWh TESS, 2.0 MWh BESS
key_results: Initial utility 92.4% (OptLayerPolicy) vs 86.1% (OptLayer); constraint-tolerance NSUM 6.1-6.5% for safety layers vs 22.3% for unsafe TD3 (Tables 3-4); about 1.9 s per step for the grey-box variant.
limitations: No formal proof; residual model mismatch; per-step solve cost; single simulated case; only TD3 tested.

authors: Jiarong Fan; Ariel Liebman; Hao Wang
problem: EV charging-station management in a distribution network under voltage constraints and solar/price uncertainty.
method: Constrained MDP solved with SAC-Lagrangian (SACL): auxiliary voltage-violation cost and a learned Lagrange multiplier; maximum-entropy exploration (Sec. III-IV).
environment_or_data: IEEE 33-bus feeder, 4 stations x 5 chargers (22 kW) with 13 kWp PV each, linearised DistFlow
key_results: Cost 926 vs 933 (SAC) and 1091 (DDPG) $; voltage-violation count 294 vs 436 and 551; unfinished demand 411.2 kWh (Table I).
limitations: Violations remain (expected-cost tolerance d); fixed four-station topology; single run without variance.

authors: Yuxiang Guan; Jin Zhang; Wenhao Ma; Liang Che
venue: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
problem: Secure EV charging control formulated as a large-scale partially observable CMDP.
method: Rule-based local and global shields embedded in the RL loop to supervise and correct agents' actions.
architecture: Multi-agent/partially observable RL with shields (details not read)
environment_or_data: IEEE 33-node system
key_results: Abstract claims strict local and global security in training and execution and a more near-optimal policy.
limitations: Abstract only; formal proof of the guarantee not verified by us; rule design is problem-specific.

authors: Javier Sales-Ortiz; Omid Ardakanian
venue: Proc. 15th ACM Int. Conf. Future and Sustainable Energy Systems (e-Energy '24)
problem: VPP trading aggregate bidirectional EV flexibility in a real-time market.
method: Aggregate EV storage so that the RL policy is independent of the number of contracts/EVs; constrain the RL action within bounds that ensure individual charging requirements; proportionally fair disaggregation to chargers.
architecture: Single aggregate RL agent + rule-based disaggregation
environment_or_data: Real-world EV dataset (details not read)
key_results: Robust performance under price uncertainty and shifts in EV mobility distribution (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only (full text blocked); whether feasibility is proven is unknown to us; aggregation hides per-EV heterogeneity in the policy.

authors: Haoyu Yan; Shutong Ding; Jiebao Zhang; Xi Yao; Yu Liu; Haoyu Wang; Chenchi Luo; Ye Shi
problem: Spatio-temporal V2G scheduling inside optimal power flow with coupled grid and EV-energy constraints.
method: HPC-RL: upper level GRG-SAC (generalised-reduced-gradient embedding, Newton completion of non-basic variables, projection of violating inequalities; Prop. 4.1 first-order feasibility); lower level 'dynamic boundary' per-EV power bounds from remaining energy and remaining intervals (Sec. 4.1-4.2, Eq. 16).
architecture: SAC with GRG layer + rule-based per-EV allocation
environment_or_data: IEEE 14-, 30- and modified 141-bus systems; 10 EVs connected per time step
baselines: MPC, penalty-based RL, optimisation-embedded RL, projection-based RL, CRL
key_results: Abstract: near-zero violation rate, nearly 100% demand satisfied, online computation reduced from hours to minutes; moderate cost gap to MPC.
limitations: Departure-energy guarantee asserted without theorem in the text we read; grid feasibility only to Newton tolerance and requires nonsingular Jacobian block; fleet size not varied; result tables not reached in our reading.

authors: Muhammad Abdullah Bin Arif; Shahid Iqbal
problem: Electric-bus depot charging on a weak 11 kV feeder with network (voltage) limits and two deadline pools.
method: Two-pool CMDP solved by a 6,165-parameter DQN; network constraint enforced by a closed-form projection applied to the action before the plant; ablation of physics-informed reward vs cost-only reward with/without the layer.
architecture: Small DQN (no ML framework) + closed-form projection
environment_or_data: Measured 11 kV connection, 94-route institutional bus fleet (Gujrat, Pakistan); 40 held-out days
baselines: Uncoordinated charging; perfect-foresight LP bound; reward-shaping ablations
key_results: Daily cost -45.0% vs uncoordinated (340,788 -> 187,335 PKR), 4.4% above LP bound; 0 voltage-floor breaches with projection across seeds/hyperparameters; reward shaping redundant once the layer is present (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; preprint (no peer review stated); exact projected constraint and any departure-energy guarantee not described in the abstract; no proof stated.

authors: Krzysztof C. Kiwiel
problem: Continuous quadratic knapsack problem (separable quadratic objective, one linear equality, box bounds) - the problem class of Euclidean projection onto a box intersected with a hyperplane.
method: Several linear-time breakpoint-searching algorithms; identifies cycling and wrong-convergence examples in existing algorithms.
environment_or_data: Large-scale computational tests
key_results: Linear-time algorithms with encouraging large-scale results (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; problem formulation details to be checked against full text before quoting specifics.

authors: Bo Wang; Lanyu Lin; Yong-Jin Liu
problem: Euclidean projection onto the intersection of a half-space and a box-like set, and its generalised Jacobian.
method: Lagrangian duality reduces the projection to a univariate semismooth equation solved by a semismooth Newton method with line-search safeguard; explicit generalised Jacobian of the projection derived.
environment_or_data: Very large-scale projection problems
key_results: Global and locally quadratic convergence; outperforms standard solvers (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; half-space (inequality) version - equality-sum case is the hyperplane special case.
